Class Work

java.lang.Object
com.eco.bio7.collection.Work
public class Work extends Object
This class offers some methods for the control of the views, perspectives and the editor area of the Bio7 application.

    • moveViewToPanel

      public static void moveViewToPanel(CustomView customView, String viewId, String panelLocation, String newTitle)
      Moves an Eclipse workbench view into a custom Bio7 panel by reparenting its SWT widget tree.

      The view is first opened the regular way in the Eclipse workbench (openView(String)). Asynchronously on the UI thread, the method then retrieves the view's e4 part model (MPart) from the part site and takes its widget — the composite the workbench passed to createPartControl(). All children of that composite (i.e. the view's actual UI) are reparented into the target Bio7 panel, a layout pass is forced, and the now-empty original view tab is hidden in the workbench.

      Note: Reparenting relies on Control.setParent(Composite), which requires platform support for reparenting. Requires a dependency on the e4 workbench model bundle (org.eclipse.e4.ui.model.workbench).

      Parameters:
      customView - the Bio7 CustomView providing the target panels; if null, the method returns without effect
      viewId - the Eclipse view ID of the view to embed (e.g. "org.eclipse.ui.console.ConsoleView"); must not be null
      panelLocation - the identifier of the target panel inside the CustomView; must not be null
      newTitle - the new title for the panel's tab; may be null to leave the tab title unchanged

    • renamePanelTab

      public static void renamePanelTab(org.eclipse.swt.widgets.Composite panelComposite, String newTitle)
      Changes the tab title of the CustomView panel that contains the given composite.

      The method climbs up the SWT widget tree starting from the given panel composite until it finds the enclosing tab container. Both CTabFolder (used by the Bio7 CustomView) and the classic TabFolder are supported. Within the folder, the tab item whose control is the panel composite itself — or an ancestor wrapper of it — is located and its text is updated.

      If the tab items report no control (i.e. getControl() returns null), the currently selected tab of the folder is renamed as a fallback. If no tab container is found at all, an error message is printed and the title remains unchanged.

      Note: This method must be called from the SWT UI thread, since it accesses and modifies widgets.

      Parameters:
      panelComposite - the composite of the CustomView panel whose tab should be renamed (as returned by CustomView.getComposite(String)); if null or disposed, the method returns without effect
      newTitle - the new text for the tab; if null, the method returns without effect and the title remains unchanged
